subject: gov.policy
name: Civil registration modernisation programme
milestone: Africa civil registration day launched on three stated pillars
position_start: The home affairs minister launched the 8th Africa civil registration day on three pillars - integration of civil registration with health, education, identity and social protection; modernisation; and decentralisation - directed at the 2030 legal identity goal
position_end: Unchanged; no further national measure, statutory instrument, coverage figure or target outturn appears in any held source, despite civil registration being described by the government as the bedrock of its digital transformation
sources: 2025-08-12 Zambia sees civil registration as bedrock of inclusive digital transformation

subject: gov.policy
name: COMESA Regional AI Strategy
milestone: Sensitisation workshop launched in Lusaka
position_start: Not established; the base carries no position on a regional AI instrument at 2025-08-01
position_end: Zambia's technology ministry, the regional secretariat and the World Bank launched the workshop in Lusaka, the first structured activity under the stakeholder engagement plan for the AI and emerging technologies consultancy; recommendations are to feed the regional AI strategy and regional digital inclusion strategy
sources: 2026-07-14 Zambia and COMESA Launch AI Initiative to Advance Regional Digital Transformation
note: Zambia is drafting a national instrument while helping shape the regional one that would frame it

subject: gov.policy
name: Data governance policy
milestone: Spatial data infrastructure policy launched with non-sensitive data open by default
position_start: A data governance framework treated as a planned component of the national electronic government plan
position_end: A sector statutory instrument under the data protection statute reviewed by stakeholders to give the health data governance framework legal force, and a spatial data policy adopted with non-sensitive data open by default

subject: gov.policy
name: Data localisation position
milestone: State operator tender for domestic storage and GPU capacity, June 2026
position_start: A cross-border transfer regime at sections 70 and 71 of the data protection statute rather than a localisation mandate
position_end: Locally hosted government workloads being procured rather than legislated: a platform partnership hosting ministry solutions in Zambia under a kwacha-denominated service agreement, and a national operator tendering for domestic storage and accelerated compute

subject: gov.policy
name: Government cloud and national data-centre capacity
milestone: Tender advertised for 150TB storage and AI/ML GPU server capacity, June 2026
position_start: A government cloud treated as a planned component of the national electronic government plan's enterprise architecture, with no standalone cloud strategy
position_end: A memorandum signed with a vendor to co-invest in a national artificial-intelligence data centre, and the state telecom operator advertising for 150TB of storage and GPU-accelerated server capacity

subject: gov.policy
name: Interoperability framework and its spatial extension
milestone: National spatial data infrastructure policy and geoportal launched, June 2026
position_start: A public service electronic government interoperability standard published in 2019
position_end: A national spatial data infrastructure policy for 2026-2030 and a national geoportal launched on open-source software, with the electronic government division as lead authority

subject: gov.policy
name: National AI Strategy
milestone: Technology ministry permanent secretary says the strategy is nearing the end of its cycle and is due for review, 2026-08-17
position_start: A parliamentary motion for an AI policy and legal framework was under public debate in July 2025; no strategy, draft or institutional home announced
position_end: A strategy text exists and is now held, which settles the question the three accounts of its stage left open: the technology ministry's statement of 2026-08-07 that the current strategy is nearing the end of its implementation cycle is consistent with the document, and the Presidential Delivery Unit's July 2026 description of one nearing completion is a reference to a successor rather than to this text. What the document cannot settle is which cycle is ending, its cover and its running headers giving horizons a year apart, and no successor draft is published
note: the successor reading of the Presidential Delivery Unit's account is an inference from the dates and is not stated in any source held; what is established is that a text exists, and that the text's own horizon is internally inconsistent

subject: gov.policy
name: National AI Strategy text
milestone: Text located and held, lodged with the OECD AI Policy Observatory April 2026
position_start: Baseline not held
position_end: The strategy text is held: a National AI Council with sector technical working groups, the Smart Zambia Institute coordinating implementation within government, the technology ministry leading adoption across the economy, and a National Emerging Technologies Centre of Excellence as the interface for international cooperation; priority sectors are agriculture, healthcare, mining, education, finance and public services, aligned to the 8th National Development Plan; data protection and ethics sit inside the governance framework rather than in a chapter of their own, with external alignment stated to the African Union's AI strategy and the UNESCO ethics recommendation and no bilateral partner named. Its implementation plan is organised by first 100 days, first year and second year rather than by calendar
note: the document carries no date of its own - no adoption date and no month in 121k characters of extracted text - and is dated here from the ministry's own launch announcement. It also disagrees with itself about its horizon: the cover reads 2024-2026 and every running header reads 2025-2027. The copy held is the one the ministry lodged with the OECD AI Policy Observatory; no first-party copy was located

subject: gov.policy
name: National broadband policy
milestone: A national event's policy working group concluded the country lacks a broadband policy
position_end: No national broadband policy; a national mapping event recommended formulating one, and delivery reporting is against connectivity coverage rather than against any adopted broadband instrument
note: a dated statement of absence by a working group convened for the purpose

subject: gov.policy
name: National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2027
milestone: Third digital economy round table, 14 May 2026
position_start: A strategy in force for 2023-2027 across five digital-transformation pillars
position_end: Implementation reported at a round table recording 94 per cent connectivity coverage, quarterly public quality-of-service reporting and K255 million approved for network-quality upgrades, with bulk international bandwidth for the government network out to bid

subject: gov.policy
name: National Information and Communication Technology Policy 2023
milestone: Sector figures published by the delivery unit, April 2026
position_start: The overarching national ICT policy in force since 2023, revising the 2006 policy
position_end: Towers grown from 3,568 in 2023 to 3,751 in 2025, average mobile population coverage at 95 per cent and 14.7 million internet subscriptions reported for 2025

subject: gov.policy
name: Open government data framework
milestone: Proactive-disclosure framework stated to be in final operationalisation, July 2026
position_start: An open government data framework treated as a planned component of the national electronic government plan
position_end: A spatial data policy adopting open by default for non-sensitive data, and the access-to-information proactive-disclosure framework covering contracts, budgets, expenditure and development projects stated to be in its final operationalisation stage

subject: gov.legislate
name: Access to Information Act, 2023
milestone: Commission guidelines issued as Government Notice No. 1624 of 2025
position_start: Act No. 24 of 2023 in force from 25 June 2024, granting a right of access to information held by an information holder
position_end: First implementing regulations supplying the request forms, fees and procedures that make the right operative, followed by rights commission guidelines translating the Act's duties into operational guidance

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cyber Security Act No. 3 of 2025, statutory text
milestone: Gazetted text acquired 2026-08-09; commenced 12 May 2025 by Statutory Instrument 22 of 2025
position_start: The statutory text was not held, so the Act’s provisions rested on secondary characterisation
position_end: Held in full. Assented 8 April 2025, published in the Supplement to the Government Gazette 15 April 2025, commenced 12 May 2025 by Statutory Instrument 22 of 2025; 66 sections in seven Parts, repealing and replacing the Cyber Security and Cyber Crimes Act 2021. Part V (sections 21 to 40) is the interception regime and is gated on a judge of the High Court
note: Acquired by the reconcile pass 2026-08-09 from the National Assembly’s own acts directory; the acquisition line for it is struck

subject: gov.legislate
name: Dedicated artificial-intelligence legislation
milestone: Readiness assessment methodology piloted at a Lusaka consultation, 22-23 June 2026
position_end: No binding artificial-intelligence instrument; a readiness assessment methodology piloted ahead of the national strategy's review before its end-2026 expiry
note: the strategy expires at the end of 2026 and no statute or regulation stands behind it

subject: gov.legislate
name: ICT (Universal Access) Regulations, 2012
milestone: Gazetted 15 June 2012
position_start: No position held on the statutory basis of Zambia's universal-access levy
position_end: Statutory Instrument No. 38 of 2012 sets the licensee contribution to the Universal Access and Service Fund at not exceeding 1.5% of gross annual turnover, capped at 50% of total collectable annual operating fees payable to the regulator, payable annually in advance; the Fund may also receive parliamentary appropriations, grants and donations. No amendment, repeal or updated rate is on record.
note: The regulatory basis for the Universal Access and Service Fund (ZMB-include.access-universal-access-service-fund); the fund's own size, current levy collected and annual disbursement remain not held

subject: gov.legislate

position_end: An amendment to the citizenship regulations, alongside the registration department computerising national registration card, passport and citizenship-document issuance with the state technology institute

subject: gov.legislate
name: Mobile money levy
milestone: Rate doubled during 2025
position_start: In force under a 2023 levy act
position_end: In force, with the rate doubled at some point in 2025; the industry levy table is stated as current to Q3 2025. No Zambian rate, base, statutory instrument, effective date or revenue outturn is held
sources: 2026-03-01 Mobile Money Taxes and Affordability in Sub-Saharan Africa
note: The doubling is dated only to the year, so it cannot be placed inside or outside the window; the source is an industry body arguing against these levies

subject: gov.legislate
name: Postal and Courier Services Bill 2026
milestone: Public written submissions closed 2026-07-27
position_start: Did not exist. Cabinet approved the review of the Postal Services Act No. 22 of 2009 in principle at its 17th meeting in September 2025, after the window opened
position_end: Ten-province stakeholder consultations concluded 2026-07-22 and a public call for written submissions closed 2026-07-27; the Bill would repeal and replace the 2009 Act, strengthen universal service obligations, modernise licensing, reinforce regulatory oversight and extend services to underserved areas through the universal access fund. No draft text, gazette notice or parliamentary date is on file
note: The 2009 Act also underwrites postal banking and financial services, so its replacement governs the postal service's agency-banking role

subject: gov.legislate
name: Startup Bill
milestone: Named by a Ministry of Technology and Science representative
position_start: Baseline not held
position_end: Named once, alongside the National AI Strategy, as an instrument through which the government would advance artificial intelligence; no text, sponsor, drafting stage, timetable or budget is held
note: The first and only mention of the Bill in the base

subject: gov.legislate
name: Statistics Act, 2018
milestone: Statutory chief executive appointed under section 11, March 2026
position_start: Act No. 13 of 2018 establishing the statistics agency and the national statistical system
position_end: The Act operating on its own terms: a release calendar for 2026 issued expressly under section 27(1), and a new Statistician-General appointed as the statutory chief executive under section 11

subject: gov.protect
name: Cabinet decision to repeal and replace the Data Protection Act 2021

subject: gov.protect

milestone: Named as part of the operative framework in the enforcement statement
position_start: In force. Project documents describe safeguards as procedural alignment with the Act, and a 2024 account records staff in over 145 offices across ten provinces requiring training on it; civil-society monitoring current to late December 2025 records Cabinet planning to repeal it
position_end: Still in force and named by the information ministry on 2026-07-18 as one of three instruments regulating online communications, cybersecurity and personal data; no repeal bill, replacement text, statutory instrument, enforcement action or penalty under the Act is held
sources: 2024-09-05-worldbank-zambia-zrhcp-pad-padhi00410|2024-09-17 DPI Safeguards come online in Zambias next phase of digital integration|2026-04-01 State of Internet Freedom in Zambia 2026 6th Edition|2026-07-21-zambia-cyber-crimes-act-enforcement-begins

position_start: Act No. 3 of 2021 establishing the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner
position_end: The Commissioner on record identifying registration as the necessary first step and naming weak internal systems and limited awareness as continuing implementation gaps

subject: gov.protect

milestone: Tender opened, bids due 2026-08-21
position_start: Not held
position_end: Out to tender under the World Bank-financed acceleration project for a digital compliance management system to serve the Data Protection Commission, to integrate with the government service bus and payment gateway and to meet ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701 and WCAG 2.1 AA; a parallel tender under the same project covers a review of the national data-protection guidelines and compliance frameworks to strengthen implementation of the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021
note: tenders rather than awards; no value, delivery date or statement of the commission's current caseload or enforcement record is held

subject: gov.protect
name: Office of the Data Protection Commissioner
milestone: Asked by nine civil society organisations to examine a beneficiary contact list, 2026-07-31
position_start: Operational, with a controller registration deadline of 2025-04-30 recorded by civil-society monitoring; no enforcement action, registration count or annual report held
position_end: Unchanged in substance. The Office formed part of a multi-sectoral delegation to the continental identity conference alongside four other institutions, in sessions covering data-protection frameworks for digital identity; no registration count, enforcement decision, fine, breach notification, guidance note or annual report is held at any date. On 2026-07-31 nine civil society organisations asked the Office to examine the source of the contact list behind SMS messages sent to Social Cash Transfer beneficiaries before the 13 August 2026 election; no response from the Office is on the record
sources: 2026-04-01 State of Internet Freedom in Zambia 2026 6th Edition|2026-05-18-zambia-id4africa-multi-sectoral-engagement|2026-07-31-civil-society-condemns-alleged-sms-linking-cash-transfers-to-voting-for-ruling-upnd
note: The regulator exists and travels; nothing in the base shows it acting

subject: gov.protect
name: Transfer of the refugee registration database to the home affairs ministry
milestone: Grant effective 2024-12-23; provided for as a project subcomponent
position_start: Provided for in the refugee and host communities project, board-approved 2024-09-26 and effective 2024-12-23, closing 2028-10-31; the appraisal document records the transfer of the agency database to the ministry on separate servers, and a US$6m identity limb enrolling refugees into the citizens' register across three districts. The only safeguard described is procedural alignment of departmental operating procedures with the Data Protection Act
position_end: Unchanged; no completion, transfer date, data-protection impact assessment, oversight arrangement or implementation status report is held
note: The safeguards framework gives US$6.5m and about 100,000 cards against the appraisal document's US$6m and about 150,000; the divergence is recorded, not resolved

subject: gov.regional

position_end: A statutory cross-border transfer regime at sections 70 and 71 of the data protection statute; no adequacy decision, transfer authorisation or enforcement action under it is held

milestone: Attributed to a regional central bank spokesperson
position_start: Baseline not held

note: A statement of intent attributed to the system's operator, not to the Zambian central bank

position_end: Elected Secretary-General at the Seventh Conference of Plenipotentiaries, taking office 2027-01-01 for a four-year term; Zambia was not elected to the 25-member Administrative Council for the coming cycle

subject: gov.standards

position_end: More than 50 international standards adopted as national standards within a catalogue of more than 6,500 national standards across sectors including information and communication technology, alongside a fourth extractives transparency validation scored at 81 points

subject: gov.standards

milestone: Issued January 2014
position_start: In force. The document states that the national electronic health record is the approved patient-level health care information system, in accordance with a circular of 5 April 2006 - the first held primary for that approval
position_end: Unchanged; no revision, replacement or superseding health-data standard is held twelve years after issue, and through the record's migration to fingerprint-based patient identity

subject: gov.standards

milestone: Issued by the state ICT institute, mandatory across government
position_start: No position held
position_end: In force and mandatory for every ministry, province and spending agency, with an annual compliance audit schedule and data management and governance requirements set alongside the electronic government statute
note: Compliance audit findings are not published

subject: gov.discourse

position_start: Not held
position_end: two independent accounts of the election period: one on the reach and risks of digital campaigning, one recording that no internet shutdown was imposed and asking why
note: preliminary statements; no final observer report, government response or electoral commission account of the accreditation and register decisions is held

position_end: The Commission's chairperson said its case review meeting considered 105 alleged human rights violations and abuses linked to the election period, of which 62 were resolved through mediation, engagement with responsible institutions, referral for legal assistance, corrective measures and other redress; duty-bearers implicated included law enforcement agencies and justice-sector institutions
note: The listed remedies are administrative, not adjudicative; no sanction, compensation or determination is reported

position_end: A nationwide constitutional consultation reporting more than 11,864 public submissions through sittings, boxes, website and email, and a bill deferred by the responsible minister after civil-society and non-governmental stakeholders raised concerns

position_end: Three-quarters of Zambians call for media freedom and a watchdog role for the media, on the survey’s own reporting
note: A survey measure of opinion, not of practice.

subject: gov.discourse
name: ZICTA consent judgment on internet access interruption
milestone: Entered after the August 2021 election-period blocking; reason for any interruption due within 36 hours
position_start: No position held on internet-shutdown constraints in Zambia at 2025-08-01
position_end: In force on the coalition's account: the regulator undertook not to act outside its authority to interrupt access and to state the reason for any future interruption within 36 hours, after civil society challenged the August 2021 blocking of four platforms; the technology ministry has committed not to shut down the internet at the 13 August 2026 election, and the government has said it could not establish the cause of the 2021 shutdown. No judgment date, cause number or enforcement instance is held
note: The judgment is known to the base only through the coalition letter; earlier disruptions are dated to 2016 and to a two-day outage in 2020 that officials attributed to heavy rain

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cyber Security Act No. 3 of 2025
milestone: Signed by the President 8 April 2025
position_start: In force; establishes the cyber security agency and a critical-information-infrastructure regime, and per the embassy alert requires providers proactively to intercept all electronic communications via a central monitoring centre
position_end: The gazetted text is now held (assented 8 April 2025, gazetted 15 April 2025, commenced 12 May 2025 by Statutory Instrument 22 of 2025), and it does not read as the secondary characterisation did. Part V gates interception on a judge: section 29 requires a law enforcement officer to apply ex-parte to a judge of the High Court for an interception of communication order, valid three months and renewable once, and section 30 permits interception without a prior order only to prevent bodily harm, loss of life or damage to property, the officer having to put the written confirmation, an affidavit, the recording and a transcript before a judge within two days. Section 21 continues the Central Monitoring and Coordination Centre as the sole facility through which lawful interception is effected, managed by the division responsible for Government communications; section 39(1)(b) obliges providers to install interception facilities “when required by a law enforcement officer or under a court order” and section 40 empowers the President to make interception-capability regulations. Section 3(1) establishes the Zambia Cyber Security Agency in the Office of the President under his general direction; “law enforcement officer” extends to any person the President designates by statutory instrument

subject: dpi.registry

subject: dpi.registry

subject: dpi.mis

subject: dpi.mis
